_about: Dogs of War's own rules as they appear in the catalogue: a short summary and the section of rules/core-rules.md that holds the full text. Rules ported from N4 are marked "n4": true and get '(N4)' after their name. Keep each summary in step with core-rules.md.

Round Structure.summary: Three rounds. Each round runs Impetuous, Pilot (pilots and their TAG), Elite Guns, Hired Guns, then Reinforcement. In each phase the player with initiative takes a full N5 Active Turn, then the other player does; only that phase's models spend Orders. The Lieutenant Order can be spent in any phase.

Order Pool.summary: Pilots and Elite Guns give Regular Orders to one pool, spent by whoever acts in the current phase. Hired Guns are Irregular and act on their own Orders in the Hired Guns phase. Track the pool with tokens: one per Regular model at the start of the round, discard one per Order spent, and at the start of each of your turns discard one per Regular model lost since your last turn.

Command Tokens.summary: The N5 starting pool, slightly enlarged (number to be set), never regained. Besides N5's uses they pay for drop pods, replacement TAGs, extra Elite Gun slots and calldowns.

Reinforcements.summary: Arrivals come in the Reinforcement phase, by the first method possible: a drop pod (1 Command Token) anywhere on the table, Deployment (Tactical), or your deployment zone. Elite Gun reserves are chosen before the game; Hired Gun reserves are unlimited. The 10-infantry cap is the only limit.

Deployment (Tactical).summary: Every reinforcing model has this skill. Place the model within the Zone of Control of an allied model and outside the LoF of every enemy.

Replacement TAGs.summary: During the Pilot phase a pilot can call in a TAG from the stock lineup, the same for every company, paid with Command Tokens (roughly most of the pool). Lineup and prices to be written.

Mount and Dismount.summary: N5 dropped this; Dogs of War brings back N4's version. Getting in: a pilot that ends a skill with the Movement label in base contact with the TAG climbs in at the end of that Order. Getting out: at the start of an Order, right after declaring its first skill with the Movement label, the pilot starts that movement anywhere in base contact with the TAG, using its own profile for the whole Order. Neither costs anything extra. Not while Engaged or Immobilized, and never through Cautious Movement from a TAG. Getting in or out cancels Hidden Deployment and marker states. Game states carry across, except Unconscious and Possessed; a Possessed TAG's pilot can't get in or out. A pilot can still leave an Unconscious TAG. While its pilot is out, the TAG acts as the pilot's Peripheral (Synchronized), staying in coherency with it or going Disconnected; while the pilot is in a Null state, the TAG is Pilotless instead. While aboard, the pilot can't be hacked or hit by E/M. N4 let pilots board only their own TAG; Dogs of War adds Jockey and Unmanned TAGs.

Jockey.summary: Pilots only. A pilot that ends any movement in base contact with an enemy TAG makes a face-to-face WIP roll against it. Results to be written.

Unmanned TAGs.summary: A pilot can climb into an enemy TAG whose pilot has dismounted, and take it over.

Pilotless State.summary: A TAG becomes Pilotless when its pilot enters a Null state (Unconscious, Dead…). It isn't a Null state itself: the TAG stays in play, counts for scoring and can be targeted. It can't generate or spend Orders, but it can still declare AROs, and its player can spend a Command Token to give it Total Reaction until Pilotless ends. Cancelled when a pilot climbs in, or when its own pilot leaves the Null state.

Eject.summary: A TAG ejects its pilot through N5's Transmutation (Escape System). The profile the TAG turns into is the company's pilot.
